title: How much change does {{NAME_2}} get back?
description: Two things are bought and paid for with one note. A bracket keeps the two costs together so they are added before they are taken from the note. Keeko doubts the bracket and takes the costs away one after the other from left to right.
teaching_notes: One idea: a bracket groups the two costs so they are added first and then taken from the note. Watch for children who write the change without the bracket and get more than the note.

source: Example 5: {{NAME_2}} bought a pack of biscuits for ₹15 and a packet of toor dal for ₹56. He gave the shopkeeper ₹100. Write an expression that can help us calculate the change he will get back.
video_script.why: The child sees why a bracket is needed when two amounts are taken away together.
video_script.substitution: Add the two costs inside a bracket and take the bracket from the note.
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_2}}'s biscuits, toor dal and one hundred rupee note at the shop
video_script.wrong_answer: one hundred minus fifteen plus fifty six
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko writes the change as one hundred minus fifteen plus fifty six and works from left to right, so the fifty six is added to the note's leftover instead of being taken away.
video_script.payoff_line: {{NAME_2}} gets back twenty nine rupees in change

final_answer.spoken: the expression is one hundred minus the bracket fifteen plus fifty six, and the change is twenty nine rupees

names.{{NAME_2}}: the child who buys biscuits and toor dal and pays with a one hundred rupee note

maths_rules: slip: 100 − 15 + 56 = 85 + 56 = 141, more than the 100 rupee note
video_script.design: One idea: a bracket groups the two costs. Assumes adding and taking away. Wrong idea: take the costs away one after the other from left to right. The shop items and the note stay all video.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='biscuit'/>{{NAME_2}} bought a pack of biscuits for fifteen rupees.
<bookmark mark='dal'/>Toor dal cost fifty six rupees, and {{NAME_2}} gave the shopkeeper one hundred rupees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How do we write the change, and how much is it?

beats.on_screen: the shop items stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a pair of curved lines ( ) drawn around the two prices, with the label bracket

marks.def: the curved lines appear around the two prices and the label bracket lands on them
marks.first: the part inside the lines glows

narration: <bookmark mark='def'/>The curved lines written around part of an expression are called a bracket.
<bookmark mark='first'/>A bracket tells us to work out what is inside it first.

beats.on_screen: Given: biscuits ₹15; toor dal ₹56; paid with ₹100
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, biscuits for fifteen rupees, toor dal for fifty six rupees, and a note of one hundred rupees.

beats.on_screen: To find: an expression for the change, and its value

marks.find: the words expression and value are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write an expression for the change, and find its value.

marks.cost: 15 + 56 is written under the two items

narration: <bookmark mark='cost'/>Step one, find what {{NAME_2}} spends. The total cost is fifteen plus fifty six.

marks.write: the bracket is drawn around 15 + 56 and taken from 100

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step two, take the total cost from the note. We put the cost in a bracket, so it is worked out first.

marks.inside: 15 + 56 is worked out and replaced by 71

narration: <bookmark mark='inside'/>Step three, work out the bracket first. Fifteen plus fifty six is seventy one.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Step four, take seventy one from one hundred, because that is what is left of the note.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>{{NAME_2}} gets back twenty nine rupees in change.
The expression is one hundred minus the bracket fifteen plus fifty six.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 100 − 15 + 56 = 141; the ₹100 note beside it is smaller than 141; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.fix: the note glows beside 141 and the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko writes one hundred minus fifteen plus fifty six. Working from left to right, that gives one hundred forty one.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But {{NAME_2}} gave only one hundred rupees, so the change cannot be more than that. The bracket keeps the two costs together.
